GC97.status: Withdraw order-only target; refine sharp coefficient
GC97.model: Unit disk \(B\subset\mathbb R^2\), \(n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\), \(0<\delta<1\), \(u\in H^2(B;\mathbb C)\) with trace \(e^{in\theta}\). Freeze \(K_1(u)=\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{Im}(\bar u\nabla u)/(1+|u|^2))\) and \(E_{\delta,n}(u)=\int_B(|\nabla u|^2+\delta^{-2}(1-|u|^2)^2+|K_1(u)|^2)\,dx\). Interior zeros are allowed.
GC97.canonical: For fixed \(n\ne0\), determine the sharp coefficient and limiting vortex geometry of \(I_n(\delta)=\inf E_{\delta,n}\) as \(\delta\downarrow0\). The weaker logarithmic-order target is already approachable with standard Ginzburg–Landau lower bounds and a smooth equivariant radial trial: \(u=f(r)e^{in\theta}\) has purely angular regularized current and \(K_1(u)=0\) distributionally. A new claim should address coefficient, \(O(1)\) corrections or minimizers, not logarithmic order alone.
GC97.resolution: Establish matching leading coefficients and a characterization of minimizers, or disprove a proposed coefficient with explicit competitors; compare the classical lower bounds to the added curvature term.
known: Classical degree-constrained vortex energy; curvature-current divergence is additional.
Serfaty, Mean field limits for Ginzburg–Landau vortices
Known vortex estimates; not a solution of the extra curvature problem.
milestones: Prove \(K_1(f(r)e^{in\theta})=0\) for a smooth admissible radial vortex.
Show \(c_n|\log\delta|\le I_n(\delta)\le C_n|\log\delta|\) by classical GL bounds and one \(H^2\) trial.
Determine whether separated unit vortices lower the leading coefficient while controlling \(\|K_1(u)\|_2^2\).
GC97.notes: Fix the classical GL normalization. Do not require nonvanishing inside B, since that would conflict with nonzero boundary winding.
GC97.recommendation: Withdraw the order-only open classification if verified; retain the sharp coefficient/geometry as a refined candidate.

GC124.model: Fix \(T_L^2=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^2\), \(L=8\pi\), \(m>0\), \(u\in H^2(T_L^2;\mathbb C)\), \(M(u)=m\), and \(E_L(u)=\int(|(\Delta+1)u|^2-\frac12|u|^4+\frac13|u|^6)\). Keep the original stripe class \(u=f(x_1)\) and fourfold-invariant localized class with \(\int_{B_{L/4}(0)}|u|^2\ge0.9m\).
GC124.canonical: For each \(m>0\) determine the sign of \(D(m)=\inf_{\mathcal A_{\rm str}(m)}E_L-\inf_{\mathcal A_{\rm loc}(m)}E_L\), classifying \(D>0,D=0,D<0\) on \((0,\infty)\). Both infima must use the same torus and mass; a nonzero infinite-plane periodic stripe has infinite \(L^2\) mass.
GC124.resolution: Prove competitor nonemptiness, finite infima and ideally attainment, then a mass-interval comparison or counterexample. Avoid interpreting restricted infima as unrestricted minimizers.
known: Whole-space splitting differs from compact-torus compactness.
Bonheure et al., mixed-dispersion standing waves
Related fourth-order model, not the exact two-class comparison.
milestones: Construct an admissible fourfold localized bump and a stripe with the same mass.
Prove coercivity and attainability of both constrained class infima on the fixed torus.
Prove a strict sign of D(m) on one explicit mass interval or give a mass with equality.
GC124.notes: The square torus supports fourfold symmetry, not continuous planar rotation; the 90% localization threshold is part of the definition.
GC124.recommendation: Retain as refined draft until a strict comparison or a comparison obstruction is proved.

GC143.status: Known spreading fact; refine quantitative tails
GC143.model: Take \(H_0=(\Delta+1)^2\) with domain \(H^4(\mathbb R^2)\), \(U(t)=e^{-itH_0}\) and nonzero \(u_0\in C_c^\infty(B_1;\mathbb C)\). For \(t\ne0\) set \(T(R,t,u_0)=\|\mathbf1_{\{|x|>R\}}U(t)u_0\|_2\).
GC143.canonical: Prove that \(U(t)u_0\) cannot be compactly supported for \(t\ne0\), using Paley–Wiener growth of the quartic Fourier phase. The potentially new question is the sharp envelope \(\sup_{\|u_0\|_{H^s}\le1,\ \operatorname{supp}u_0\subset B_1,\ t\in[t_0,t_1]}T(R,t,u_0)\) for prescribed \(s>0\) and \(0<t_0<t_1\), as \(R\to\infty\).
GC143.resolution: Separate the classical qualitative no-finite-propagation proof from two-sided quantitative tails for the fully specified data class.
known: Classical exponential-type obstruction, applied to the exact quartic multiplier.
Li, Soffer and Yao, fourth-order Schrödinger decay
milestones: Use the multiplier \(e^{-it(1-|\xi|^2)^2}\) to prove that two compact supports at distinct times force zero data.
Prove one explicit class-uniform off-support upper bound.
Construct lower-tail examples ruling out an overly strong universal decay rate.
GC143.notes: Compactly supported C-infinity data without a bounded norm or Gevrey class do not define one universal sharp tail exponent.
GC143.recommendation: Treat the qualitative question as known and keep only the quantitative tail problem.

Use \(L_\phi(\theta)=2-[1+(\nabla+i\theta)^2]^2-3\phi^2\) with \(\theta\in[-1/2,1/2]^2\) and domain \(H^4(T^2)\).
GC177.canonical: Characterize profiles satisfying \(\sup_{\theta\ne0}\sup\operatorname{Re}\sigma(L_\phi(\theta))\le0\), including neutral translation and the small-\(\theta\) Bloch expansion. The quasi-momentum is continuous because the medium is infinite periodic.
GC177.resolution: First prove a nonzero stripe branch, then a complete quasi-momentum spectral criterion or an explicit unstable sideband.
